title: Make a new kind of parcel impossible to quote by accident

blocks.text: The web shop quotes shipping with the carrier's parcel types, `Letter`, `Box` and `Tube`. Prices in cents:

rows: 650, plus 120 for each started kilogram, plus 400 if it is fragile

blocks.text: `Parcel` and its records come from the carrier's library, and the carrier adds a kind of parcel once or twice a year. The last time, the shop quoted the new kind at a price nobody had agreed, for a month, at a loss on every one.
Write `priceCents(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ParcelPricing.java`, without touching the hierarchy. When the next kind arrives, two things must hold:

items: once the shop is built against the new library, the build fails, with the compiler pointing at your method;
a copy of the shop built before the new kind existed, which meets one in production, throws rather than quoting any price.

blocks.text: About five lines in total. The tests compile your file themselves, once as it is and once with a kind added, and run the old build against the new hierarchy.

cases.says: letters, boxes and tubes get the prices the table gives them
once a kind of parcel is added to the hierarchy, the class no longer compiles, and the error is that the switch doesn't cover every input
a build compiled before a kind was added still prices the old kinds and throws for the new one rather than quoting a price

origin.section: A Subtype Added After Compilation Reaches the Switch as MatchException

concepts: A switch with no default, compiled before a permitted subtype was added, throws MatchException when it meets that subtype; a default answers it instead.
Over a sealed type, an unguarded case for each permitted subtype makes the switch exhaustive with no default, so a new subtype stops the build at the switch, while a default absorbs it silently.
